about: Flagship stories are the executable spec. Atlas stories expand every persona, job, and constraint into a reviewable requirement. Oriel is the window. Grok Bot, Dots, and Muse stay themselves.

stories.persona: a person with more than one agent
stories.title: A first goal convenes the seats that are on
stories.story: As a person with more than one agent, I want Oriel to convene the seats I have switched on and answer in one voice, so that I am not the router between them.
acceptance: Sending a goal creates one goal in the record.
The spoken reply names exactly one seat as the lead.
Only enabled, eligible seats appear as reads.
stories.sourceInsight: The shared pattern is an agent with its own computer and browser that keeps going after the laptop closes.

stories.title: An outbound send is held
stories.story: As a sales lead, I want Oriel to draft the follow-up and hold the send, so that a message cannot leave before I have seen it.
acceptance: An email request creates an open approval titled Release a send.
The draft names any person Oriel could extract.
No reply claims the message was delivered.
stories.sourceInsight: All three ask before sensitive actions, and all three vendors still describe prompt injection as unsolved.

stories.title: An explicit do-not-send is skipped
stories.story: As a founder, I want Oriel to treat a request that says do not send as the instruction, so that the draft finishes without an approval.
acceptance: The send step is skipped, not left open.
The voice says the send was left unsent because it was ruled out.
The goal finishes with no approval still open.
stories.sourceInsight: A shared bot computer and a perpetual grant are how one mistake spreads. Oriel approves once and does not offer always-allow.

stories.title: Denying a hold releases nothing
stories.story: As a marketer, I want Oriel's Not now to close the hold without publishing, so that a change of mind is final until I ask again.
acceptance: The approval status becomes denied when the person says not now.
The reply tells the person that nothing was released.
A second decision on the same hold is rejected.
stories.sourceInsight: A shared bot computer and a perpetual grant are how one mistake spreads. Oriel approves once and does not offer always-allow.

stories.title: A preference is recalled later
stories.story: As a chief of staff, I want to say what to keep and ask for it later, so that Oriel does not reset between turns.
acceptance: A remember-only turn stores the preference and does not open a goal.
A later recall lists that same preference back.
The preference survives in public state.
stories.sourceInsight: Dots, announced by OpenAI on 29 September 2026, is one always-on owner agent on GPT-6 Astra that keeps working between conversations.

stories.title: A switched-off seat is not convened
stories.story: As an engineer, I want Oriel to move the work to the next capable seat when I switch one off, so that a vendor being unavailable does not stop the job.
acceptance: The switched-off seat is named in the why.
The lead is a seat that is still switched on.
The switched-off seat is not given a read.
stories.sourceInsight: Grok Bot is the seat with published team controls. Dots rides ChatGPT plans. Muse is a consumer agent without an admin console.

stories.title: A saved routine still obeys holds
stories.story: As an operations manager, I want Oriel to save a workflow and run it again, so that repetition does not become a way around a hold.
acceptance: Saving the same instruction twice does not duplicate the routine.
Running it creates a new goal from that instruction.
A do-not-send inside the instruction is still skipped.
stories.sourceInsight: Grok Bot, launched in beta on 11 August 2026, is a team of named bots on one shared cloud computer, with skills, routines, and an approval gate.

stories.title: Open holds and watches are waiting on return
stories.story: As a parent, I want to come back to Oriel and see what is waiting, so that an always-on agent does not hide unfinished work.
acceptance: An open payment appears as Waiting on you.
A keep-an-eye loop appears on the return card as a watch.
Settling the payment removes that line and leaves the watch.
After a later goal with no hold, the earlier open hold can still be settled from the return card.
stories.sourceInsight: Dots, announced by OpenAI on 29 September 2026, is one always-on owner agent on GPT-6 Astra that keeps working between conversations.

stories.title: A bridge token never enters public state
stories.story: As a security admin, I want to attach a bridge token in Oriel without seeing it come back, so that the window is not a second copy of the secret.
acceptance: Public state reports hasToken and omits the token string.
The ledger says a token was updated and does not include it.
state.json on disk does not contain the token.
stories.sourceInsight: A buyer still needs a record of who was convened, what was held, and what was released. That record is Oriel's job.

stories.title: A failed live bridge falls back and says so
stories.story: As an operator, I want Oriel to name a dead bridge while the reference read continues, so that a vendor outage is visible and the work is not invented as live.
acceptance: The seat read starts with the live bridge failure.
After the failure, the seat mode is reference.
The connector records the bridge result as fallback.
stories.sourceInsight: The shared pattern is an agent with its own computer and browser that keeps going after the laptop closes.

stories.title: Every payment is held and never executed here
stories.story: As a finance lead, I want Oriel to stop any purchase for approval, and I want releasing it to record consent without moving money.
acceptance: A stated dollar amount opens a payment hold.
Approving it says Oriel did not move money.
The reply never claims a charge was made.
stories.sourceInsight: Muse, launched by Meta on 8 September 2026, is a personal agent in its own VM, reached like a message, with a Sentinel check before sensitive actions.

stories.title: Every deletion is held
stories.story: As an operations manager, I want Oriel to stop a delete request for approval, so that a phrase in chat cannot erase work.
acceptance: The hold is titled Release a deletion before anything is removed.
The detail says nothing is deleted from here.
Denying the hold leaves its status denied.
stories.sourceInsight: A shared bot computer and a perpetual grant are how one mistake spreads. Oriel approves once and does not offer always-allow.

stories.title: A real disagreement is shown
stories.story: As a product designer, I want Oriel to show when seats would do the work differently, so that a single voice does not hide a real split.
acceptance: A personal task that also asks for a calendar names both Muse and Grok Bot.
The dissent says Oriel will not schedule anything unless a routine is saved.
The recommendation still names one lead.
stories.sourceInsight: Grok Bot, launched in beta on 11 August 2026, is a team of named bots on one shared cloud computer, with skills, routines, and an approval gate.

stories.title: Client work stays off the consumer seat
stories.story: As a law-firm partner, I want Oriel to keep client work off Muse, so that a consumer agent is not where a matter lands.
acceptance: Muse is not given a seat read on client work.
The why says confidential work stays off a consumer seat.
Grok Bot leads this work when that seat is switched on.
stories.sourceInsight: Grok Bot is the seat with published team controls. Dots rides ChatGPT plans. Muse is a consumer agent without an admin console.

stories.title: User text is shown as text
stories.story: As a security admin, I want anything I type to stay text in Oriel's thread, so that a message cannot become markup.
acceptance: A string that looks like an image tag is visible as text.
The document contains no element created from that string.
The composer still accepts a normal follow-up.
stories.sourceInsight: All three ask before sensitive actions, and all three vendors still describe prompt injection as unsolved.

stories.title: There is no always-allow
stories.story: As a security admin, I want Oriel to approve each risky action once, so that a standing grant cannot outlive the decision.
acceptance: The interface has no always-allow control.
Approving one hold does not approve a later hold of the same kind.
The ledger records each settlement separately.
stories.sourceInsight: A shared bot computer and a perpetual grant are how one mistake spreads. Oriel approves once and does not offer always-allow.

stories.title: The record names who was convened
stories.story: As an executive, I want Oriel's record to say which seats were convened, so that a later review does not depend on the chat scrollback.
acceptance: A convened event lists the names of the seats.
The desk brief includes that same record.
The convened event survives in public state.
stories.sourceInsight: A buyer still needs a record of who was convened, what was held, and what was released. That record is Oriel's job.

stories.title: A short preference collapses the brief
stories.story: As a chief of staff, I want a stored preference for short briefs to collapse Oriel's working card, so that the voice stays one paragraph.
acceptance: After the preference is stored, the next brief is marked tight.
The voice is still the recommendation, not a model essay.
A prose rewriter is not called while the brief is tight.
stories.sourceInsight: Dots, announced by OpenAI on 29 September 2026, is one always-on owner agent on GPT-6 Astra that keeps working between conversations.

stories.title: A cadence wakes one routine and still holds the risky step
stories.story: As an operations manager, I want Oriel to wake a saved routine when its cadence is due, so that the work continues while I am away and a hold still stops the risky part.
acceptance: A manual routine does not run when Oriel wakes the desk.
When more than one routine is due, only the earliest one runs.
A send inside the woken routine stays open, and the wake does not approve it.
stories.sourceInsight: Grok Bot, launched in beta on 11 August 2026, is a team of named bots on one shared cloud computer, with skills, routines, and an approval gate.

stories.title: A bridge can be checked without doing the work
stories.story: As an operator, I want Oriel to check that a bridge I control is reachable before it hands over work, so that a dead endpoint is obvious and nothing is sent while I check.
acceptance: A seat with no bridge URL cannot be checked.
A reachable bridge is marked live and the reply says nothing was sent or spent.
The bridge token is absent from the spoken reply and from public state.
stories.sourceInsight: The shared pattern is an agent with its own computer and browser that keeps going after the laptop closes.

stories.title: Pausing wakes leaves the hold untouched
stories.story: As a chief of staff, I want Oriel to pause scheduled wakes without deleting the routine, so that the desk can be quiet and a hold still waits for me.
acceptance: A due routine does not run while wakes are paused, and its next time stays where it was.
Pausing does not approve an open hold, send mail, or move money.
Resuming does not release a hold, and the next wake still stops for one.
stories.sourceInsight: Dots, announced by OpenAI on 29 September 2026, is one always-on owner agent on GPT-6 Astra that keeps working between conversations.

stories.title: A skill is the method and does not wake
stories.story: As an operations manager, I want Oriel to save a demonstrated path as a skill and apply it to a new request, so that the method travels without becoming a schedule.
acceptance: Saving the same method twice does not duplicate the skill.
A skill has no cadence and does not run when Oriel wakes the desk.
Applying the skill keeps a do-not-send from the method, and applying it does not approve a hold.
stories.sourceInsight: Grok Bot, launched in beta on 11 August 2026, is a team of named bots on one shared cloud computer, with skills, routines, and an approval gate.

stories.title: A hold raised while you were away expires
stories.story: As a security admin, I want Oriel to expire a hold raised by a routine when I am away, so that a late answer cannot run the action and there is still no always-allow.
acceptance: A hold from a turn I am in waits until I answer, and approving it later still does not send mail or move money.
A hold raised by a woken routine expires after ten minutes, and approving it then does not call the bridge or run the action.
The expired card offers no always-allow. Asking again opens a new hold that still waits for me.
stories.sourceInsight: A shared bot computer and a perpetual grant are how one mistake spreads. Oriel approves once and does not offer always-allow.

stories.persona: a person who already has a password
stories.title: A password change is handed to you
stories.story: As a person who already has a password, I want Oriel to hand a password change or a sign-in to me, so that a seat never types the secret.
acceptance: Changing a password opens a handoff and does not open a credential approval a seat could run.
Marking the step done does not call the bridge, send mail, or move money.
A pasted password is redacted, and approving the handoff is not how the step gets done.
stories.sourceInsight: Dots, announced by OpenAI on 29 September 2026, is one always-on owner agent on GPT-6 Astra that keeps working between conversations.

stories.title: A handoff rule names the step that stays yours
stories.story: As a security admin, I want Oriel to save a handoff rule for a named action from the rail, so that a later request which would do that action is mine and a seat never runs it.
acceptance: Saving the same named action twice does not duplicate the rule, and the rule does not wake or approve a hold.
A later deletion is handed to you, and a draft that would not delete does not open a handoff.
Marking the step done does not call the bridge or send mail, and there is still no always-allow.
stories.sourceInsight: A shared bot computer and a perpetual grant are how one mistake spreads. Oriel approves once and does not offer always-allow.

stories.title: A handoff rule can name the words that stay yours
stories.story: As a security admin, I want Oriel to let a handoff rule name a phrase, so that only a request that mentions those words is mine and every other request stays a hold.
acceptance: Saving the same phrase twice does not duplicate the rule, and a different phrase updates that one rule.
A deletion that omits the phrase is held, and a deletion that includes the phrase is handed to you.
Marking the step done does not call the bridge, and there is still no always-allow.
stories.sourceInsight: A shared bot computer and a perpetual grant are how one mistake spreads. Oriel approves once and does not offer always-allow.

stories.title: A sentence can name the words that stay yours
stories.story: As a security admin, I want to tell Oriel which words hand a deletion to me, so that the sentence saves the rule and does not itself delete anything.
acceptance: Saying the same words twice saves one rule, and a different phrase updates that rule instead of adding a second.
The sentence does not open a handoff, call a bridge, or approve a hold that is already open.
A later deletion that mentions the words is handed to you, and a sentence that would not delete does not save a rule or open a card.
stories.sourceInsight: Dots, announced by OpenAI on 29 September 2026, is one always-on owner agent on GPT-6 Astra that keeps working between conversations.

stories.title: A sentence can clear the words that stay yours
stories.story: As a security admin, I want to tell Oriel to stop handing a deletion that mentions certain words to me, so that the sentence clears that rule and does not itself delete anything.
acceptance: Saying the saved words clears that one rule, and words that are not the saved phrase leave the rule in place.
The sentence does not open a handoff, call a bridge, approve a hold, send mail, or move money.
A sentence that would delete is not a clear, and there is still no always-allow.
stories.sourceInsight: Dots, announced by OpenAI on 29 September 2026, is one always-on owner agent on GPT-6 Astra that keeps working between conversations.

stories.title: A sentence can clear a handoff that names no words
stories.story: As a security admin, I want to tell Oriel to stop handing deletions to me, so that a rule with no phrase is cleared and a rule that names other words stays.
acceptance: Saying stop handing deletions to me clears a deletion rule that has no phrase, and it leaves a rule that names other words in place.
The sentence does not open a handoff, call a bridge, approve a hold, send mail, or move money.
A sentence that would delete is not a clear, and there is still no always-allow.
stories.sourceInsight: A shared bot computer and a perpetual grant are how one mistake spreads. Oriel approves once and does not offer always-allow.

stories.title: A sentence can read which steps are handed to you
stories.story: As a security admin, I want to ask Oriel what is handed to me, so that it names each saved rule and does not itself delete, send, or spend.
acceptance: Asking what is handed to me names every saved rule, and it says so when none are saved.
A deletion with no phrase is the whole deletion, and a phrase such as shared project files is only those words.
The sentence does not open a card, call a bridge, save or clear a rule, approve a hold, send mail, or move money.
stories.sourceInsight: Dots, announced by OpenAI on 29 September 2026, is one always-on owner agent on GPT-6 Astra that keeps working between conversations.

stories.title: A sentence can ask whether one step is handed to you
stories.story: As a security admin, I want to ask Oriel whether a deletion is handed to me, so that it names only that rule and does not mention the others or delete anything.
acceptance: Asking whether a deletion is handed to me names only that rule, and it says so when that action has no rule.
A deletion with no phrase is the whole deletion, and a phrase such as shared project files is only those words.
The sentence does not open a card, call a bridge, save or clear a rule, approve a hold, send mail, or move money.
stories.sourceInsight: A shared bot computer and a perpetual grant are how one mistake spreads. Oriel approves once and does not offer always-allow.

stories.title: A sentence can ask whether the saved words are the ones
stories.story: As a security admin, I want to ask Oriel whether a deletion that mentions certain words is handed to me, so that it names only that match and does not delete anything.
acceptance: Asking whether a deletion mentions those words names only that rule when the phrase matches.
A rule with no phrase is not those words, and a different saved phrase is named instead of the asked words.
The sentence does not open a card, call a bridge, save or clear a rule, approve a hold, send mail, or move money.
stories.sourceInsight: Dots, announced by OpenAI on 29 September 2026, is one always-on owner agent on GPT-6 Astra that keeps working between conversations.

stories.title: A sentence can ask which words a step uses
stories.story: As a security admin, I want to ask Oriel which words a deletion hands to me, so that it names only that phrase and does not delete anything.
acceptance: Asking which words a deletion hands to me names only that rule's phrase, and a rule with no phrase says it names no words.
If that action has no rule, Oriel says so and does not mention the other rules.
The sentence does not open a card, call a bridge, save or clear a rule, approve a hold, send mail, or move money.
stories.sourceInsight: A shared bot computer and a perpetual grant are how one mistake spreads. Oriel approves once and does not offer always-allow.

stories.title: A sentence can ask which step uses certain words
stories.story: As a security admin, I want to ask Oriel which step mentions certain words, so that it names only those rules and does not delete anything.
acceptance: Asking which step mentions those words names only the actions whose phrase is those words, including more than one.
A rule with no phrase is not those words, and if none match Oriel says so without naming the other rules.
The sentence does not open a card, call a bridge, save or clear a rule, approve a hold, send mail, or move money.
stories.sourceInsight: Dots, announced by OpenAI on 29 September 2026, is one always-on owner agent on GPT-6 Astra that keeps working between conversations.

stories.story: As a security admin, I want to ask Oriel which steps name no words, so that it names only those rules and does not delete anything.
acceptance: Asking which steps name no words names only the actions whose rules have no phrase, including more than one.
A rule that names words is left out, and its phrase is not quoted. If none are phrase-less, Oriel says so.
The sentence does not open a card, call a bridge, save or clear a rule, approve a hold, send mail, or move money.
stories.sourceInsight: A shared bot computer and a perpetual grant are how one mistake spreads. Oriel approves once and does not offer always-allow.

stories.title: A sentence can ask which steps name words

acceptance: Asking which steps name words names only the actions whose rules have a phrase, and quotes each phrase.
A rule with no phrase is left out and is not described as the whole action. If none name words, Oriel says so.
The sentence does not open a card, call a bridge, save or clear a rule, approve a hold, send mail, or move money.
stories.sourceInsight: A shared bot computer and a perpetual grant are how one mistake spreads. Oriel approves once and does not offer always-allow.

stories.title: A sentence can ask which steps share words

acceptance: Asking which steps share words names only the actions whose phrase matches another rule, and quotes that phrase on each.
A phrase used once is left out, and a rule with no phrase is not described as the whole action. If none share, Oriel says so.
The sentence does not open a card, call a bridge, save or clear a rule, approve a hold, send mail, or move money.
stories.sourceInsight: A shared bot computer and a perpetual grant are how one mistake spreads. Oriel approves once and does not offer always-allow.

stories.title: A sentence can ask which words are shared

acceptance: Asking which words are shared names only a phrase used by more than one rule, once, and names the actions that use it.
A phrase used once is left out, and a rule with no phrase is not described as the whole action. If none share, Oriel says so.

acceptance: Asking which steps do not share words names only the actions whose phrase is used by exactly one rule, and quotes that phrase on each.

Oriel must make sure that saying pause or resume and one routine's name pauses or resumes that one wake, leaves the cadence and the next time, and does not run the routine, so that I get an itinerary without a booking I did not confirm.

The constraint holds for this story: saying pause or resume and one routine's name pauses or resumes that one wake, leaves the cadence and the next time, and does not run the routine.
The rule does not wake, does not approve a hold, and does not run the action. A request that would not do that action does not open a handoff.
Pause the Launch note routine leaves that cadence and the next time. Resume clears only that pause. A desk pause does not mark the routine. Nothing is run, sent, or spent.
